## Mechanic Signature

| field | design |
| --- | --- |
| wonder_specific_hook | The red palace, Gate of Justice, water courts, treaty rolls, translators, protected households, and foreign observers make the Alhambra a test of whether victory can become governed surrender. |
| core_interaction_loop | The player opens the treaty court, waits for or checks a real war-validation window, chooses mercy, tribute, or deterrence clauses, and handles whether the palace looks protected or merely occupied. |
| player_decision_pattern | Choices decide which settlement terms define the reward and whether defeated elites, royal treasury, envoys, artisans, or garrison officers absorb the cost. |
| state_feedback_model | The incident log tracks the war validation and treaty crisis while the checklist tracks whether key clauses have been witnessed and preserved. |
| failure_or_tension_model | A threatened palace, dishonored safe-conduct, or harsh settlement forces repair, hostage guarantees, or a humbled dedication with weaker diplomatic reach. |
| reward_expression | The reward expresses prestige and diplomatic reputation earned from a visible, enforceable capitulation rather than raw conquest. |
| reuse_risk_mitigation | This design belongs to Granada's surrender palace; ordinary palaces do not combine war outcome, protected court artistry, waterworks, symbolic keys, and foreign treaty witnesses. |
